newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.S. warns against Angolan intervention in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns against Angolan intervention in Zaire.

text.p: The United States has delivered an enigmatic warning against involvement by any Angolan parties in the fighting in Zaire.

But U.S. spokesmen declined to say which Angolans -- the government or former UNITA rebels -- were the main target of the warning or whether the intervention might be on the side of Zaire's government or the ethnic Tutsis it is battling in the east of the country.
Since Angola's northern border adjoins southern Zaire, far from the scene of the conflict, it seemed likely the United States was warning the Angolan government not to aid the government of Zaire.

The reluctance of U.S. officials to provide more information prompted speculation that the warning, dropped into a Security Council speech on Thursday by U.S. Ambassador Bill Richardson, might have been based on intelligence that Washington was not prepared to disclose.

Richardson's speech was about the situation in Angola, where the Security Council has held UNITA largely responsible for repeated delays in forming a national unity government with the administration of President Jose Eduardo dos Santos as the culmination of a 1994 peace accord.

After saying the "benefits of peace must replace the constantly delayed hopes of the people of Angola," Richardson continued: "We would also warn the parties against any involvement in the conflict of Zaire."

He reaffirmed a recent statement by the Security Council president calling on all states in the region to refrain from any act including cross-border incursions that would threaten the sovereignty and territorial integrity of any state.
